name: Foundations
description: What accessibility QA is, how the standards and the law are structured, how barriers get built, and why an automated scan finds only a fraction of what matters.

name: Assistive Technology Fluency
description: Operating screen readers, magnification, switch access and voice control well enough to review with them rather than about them — the specific failures a lived-experience reviewer catches that a scanner misses.

name: Cognitive, Content and Energy Accessibility
description: The barriers WCAG covers thinly: cognitive load, unclear content, sensory load, and interfaces that cost more energy than a person has.

name: Running a Real Audit
description: Scoping, evidence, severity and reporting — the practical craft of an audit a development team can actually work from, not a list of violation codes.

name: Advocacy & Organisational Change
description: Turning audit findings into shipped fixes: making the case internally, working with design and engineering, and the difference between compliance theatre and a genuine accessibility practice.

name: Working in Accessibility
description: Getting and holding accessibility work — employed, contract or freelance — and structuring it so it doesn't cost more than it pays.
